issues.detail: The Greek 'πληρωσεις' is a second-person singular verb ('you will fill'), but the Vietnamese 'Cũng sẽ làm cho tôi đầy' translates it as a third-person action or a general statement. The subject of the action in Greek is the one being addressed (the 'You' of the poem), not a third party like 'Chúa' (Lord) who is the subject of the first clause.
The Vietnamese translation shifts the subject from 2nd person ('you') to 3rd person ('Chúa' - Lord) for the second clause, which is not present in the Greek text.
